drafts.caption_zh:
Citizens 的金融科技研究主管 Devin Ryan 舉了一個對比:一個現在一個月交易 2 次的散戶,把帳戶接上 AI 代理人之後,可能變成一天交易 20 次。

這已經不是假設。7 月底美國財經媒體整理了正在發生的事:Robinhood 近期推出讓第三方 AI 代理人連進客戶帳戶的工具;券商 Public 自己養代理人來自動化投資流程;新創 Podium Markets AI 的助理 Ivy 會跨多個券商帳戶看你的持股,再依你的目標和風險承受度給建議。

但整篇報導最值得抄下來的,不是這些功能,而是這幾家的共同底線——

▸ Podium 共同創辦人兼執行長 Dirk Mueller-Ingrand:「The AI informs, but the human decides.」(AI 提供資訊,人做決定)
▸ Public 共同創辦人兼共同執行長 Leif Abraham:「You still have the last word.」(最後一句話還是你說)。Public 要求用戶先審核並批准代理人的工作流程,代理人才會去執行任何投資任務。

翻成散戶聽得懂的話:代理人時代變貴的不是下單速度,是「你按下確認之前到底懂多少」。交易次數從一個月 2 次變成一天 20 次,不會讓每一筆的資訊落差自己縮小,只會讓同一個落差被重複更多次。

所以真正要練的是那道人工閘門。三件現在就能開始做的事:
1️⃣ 先寫下「不做條件」——什麼情況你不加碼,而不是什麼情況你要買。
2️⃣ 讓 AI 幫你蒐集與整理,不讓它幫你下結論;它給的每個數字都回原始出處對一次。
3️⃣ 任何自動化都留一道人工確認——報導裡連券商自己都是這樣設計的。

MarketDaily 做的就是那道閘門前面的功課:週一到週六(週日休息)早上 7 點寄台股日報、晚上 20:00 寄美股晚報,只寫跟你持股有關的部分,判斷錯的一樣照列不刪。目前限時免費開放;未來恢復收費後,現在訂閱的早鳥用戶永久保留免費使用權。

drafts.caption_en:
Devin Ryan, head of financial technology research at Citizens, framed it like this: a retail investor who trades twice a month today could end up placing 20 trades in a single day once an AI agent is wired into the account.

This is not hypothetical anymore. US financial media laid out in late July what is already shipping: Robinhood recently launched tools that let third-party AI agents connect to customer accounts; the brokerage Public is building agents in-house to automate investing workflows; and startup Podium Markets AI has an assistant, Ivy, that reviews your holdings across multiple brokerage accounts and makes recommendations based on your goals and risk tolerance.

The most quotable part of that coverage is not the features, though. It is the common floor all of them set:

- Dirk Mueller-Ingrand, co-founder and CEO of Podium: "The AI informs, but the human decides."
- Leif Abraham, co-founder and co-CEO of Public: "You still have the last word." Public requires users to review and approve an agent's workflow before it carries out any investing task.

Translated for the rest of us: what gets expensive in the agent era is not order speed, it is how much you understand before you hit confirm. Going from two trades a month to 20 trades a day does not shrink the information gap on any single decision. It just repeats the same gap more times.

So the thing worth training is that human checkpoint. Three things you can start today:
1. Write down your do-not-act conditions first - what would stop you adding to a position, not what would make you buy.
2. Let AI gather and organise; do not let it conclude. Check every number it hands you against the original source.
3. Keep a human confirmation step in front of any automation - in that coverage, even the brokers build it that way.

MarketDaily does the homework that sits in front of that checkpoint: the Taiwan-market brief lands at 7am and the US wrap at 20:00, Monday to Saturday (Sunday off), covering only what touches your own holdings, and the calls we got wrong stay on the record. 只多加 1 句指令,AI 就從「報喜不報憂」變成「列出 3 個看空理由」。

多數人問 AI 的方式,注定只會拿到附和自己的答案——你問「這檔看起來不錯吧?」,它就順著你講下去。要拿到有用的東西,得先把它的立場改掉。

📋 直接複製這段(把 [股票代號] 換成你自己的持股):

「你現在是空方研究員,任務不是安慰我。針對 [股票代號],列出 3 個具體的看空理由,每一個都標明依據屬於哪一類:財報、產業結構、籌碼、還是總體環境。接著指出這 3 個理由裡,你自己最不確定的假設是哪一個。最後告訴我:要出現什麼樣的新證據,才會讓你收回這個看空。不要提供任何進出價位,只講風險邏輯。」

為什麼這樣問才有用:
1️⃣ 先指定立場 → 切掉模型討好你的預設反應
2️⃣ 要求標註依據類別 → 一眼看出哪條是硬資料、哪條只是它在推測
3️⃣ 要求寫出「推翻條件」→ 你拿到的是一張可以追蹤的檢查清單,而不是一段感想

⚠️ 提醒:AI 產出的是待驗證的問題清單,不是結論。它會把數字講錯,每個數據都回原始財報對一次。

Most people ask AI in a way that only ever produces agreement. Ask "this one looks decent, right?" and it will happily agree with you. To get something useful, change its stance first.

📋 Copy this (swap [TICKER] for a stock you actually hold):

"You are now a short-side research analyst. Your job is not to reassure me. For [TICKER], list 3 specific bear cases. Finally: what new evidence would make you withdraw this bear case? Do not give me any entry or exit prices, only the risk logic."

Why this works:
1️⃣ Assigning a stance strips out the model's default urge to please you
2️⃣ Labeling the evidence type shows at a glance what is hard data and what is guesswork
3️⃣ Asking for falsification conditions turns the answer into a checklist you can track, not an opinion
